sections.overview: Xysticus lanio is a crab spider recorded across Europe and parts of western and central Asia.
sections.identification: Females are pale brown with dark markings; males are darker and reddish, with a patterned abdomen.
sections.habitat: It is associated mainly with deciduous and mixed woodland, especially oak woods and their edges.
sections.diet: It waits for insects and sometimes smaller spiders, then seizes them with its front legs.
sections.behavior: This ambush hunter commonly sits on low branches, shrubs or leaves rather than hunting on the ground.
sections.reproduction: The female guards an egg sac in summer; the young spiders overwinter.
sections.ecology: Adults are reported mainly from spring to midsummer in the central-European account.
sections.conservation: The World Spider Catalog recognizes Xysticus lanio as an accepted species.
